title: How the three-room house tour was made
intro: The actual sequence from one Blender house to three illustrated room views: gray geometry, whole-atlas attempts, continuous-panorama repair, then deterministic runtime projection. This report exposes the executed prompts and ordered inputs; it does not describe a new artwork fix.
overview: The actual sequence from one Blender house to three illustrated room views: gray geometry, whole-atlas attempts, continuous-panorama repair, then deterministic runtime projection. This report exposes the executed prompts and ordered inputs; it does not describe a new artwork fix.

rooms.summary: Broad table/floor and ceiling joins now coherent; faint wall bands and approximate fixture proportions remain.

steps.title: 1. Render the actual Blender room
steps.summary: Camera [-1.3, -1.3, 1.15] m. Six 90° views are assembled into one 3072×2048 atlas: front/right/back above left/up/down. Front door closed; both internal doors open 75°. Existing polygonal wall facets and proxy silhouettes are visible in this guide and are inherited by the illustration; this process does not redesign or smooth the model.

notes: Gray facets belong to the existing modeled room and remained in the guide; these calls did not remodel the house.
All nine executed imagegen calls operated on a whole atlas or a whole panorama, never six independent face generations.
The prepared bedroom-v2 atlas revision was not executed; the continuous strategy replaced it.
Full prompts are the original text files, with SHA-256; reference roles distinguish geometry from style.
Reprojection checks certify mapping, not absence of painted seams or exact geometry.
